content.value_statement: Server-side CloudBase auth work can mix caller identity, user lookup, and custom login details. This skill guides Node.js agents through correct SDK methods and secure backend patterns.
actual_capabilities: Initialize CloudBase Node SDK auth in backend functions and services.
Read current caller identity with getUserInfo for authorization decisions.
Look up CloudBase users by uid or login identifier.
Issue custom login tickets for existing user systems.
Apply guidance for client IP logging and sensitive data handling.
Route provider setup, web login UI, and raw HTTP auth work to the right skills.
limitations: Does not configure CloudBase auth providers or publishable keys.
Does not build frontend login or sign-up interfaces.
Does not document raw HTTP auth endpoints.
Requires official CloudBase SDK documentation for APIs outside the listed methods.

use_cases.title: Authorize Cloud Functions
use_cases.description: Read caller identity in a CloudBase function and use uid or customUserId for access checks.

use_cases.title: Inspect User Records
use_cases.description: Query CloudBase end-user profiles from trusted server-side admin tools.

use_cases.title: Bridge Existing Accounts
use_cases.description: Create custom login tickets after an external user system authenticates a user.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Current Caller
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a CloudBase function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth-nodejs-cloudbase skill to show how my Node CloudBase function can read the current caller identity and choose the right user identifier.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up a User
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for trusted backend lookup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth-nodejs-cloudbase skill to design a trusted Node backend flow that looks up a CloudBase user by uid, phone, email, or custom user ID.

prompt_templates.title: Issue Custom Tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth-nodejs-cloudbase skill to create a Node-side custom login ticket flow for users authenticated by my existing account system.

prompt_templates.title: Review Auth Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth-nodejs-cloudbase skill to review my CloudBase Node auth plan for backend-only responsibilities, sensitive logging, and client handoff boundaries.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how a CloudBase function can know who called it.
output_examples.output: The response explains when to use getUserInfo, which identifiers matter, and how to apply authorization checks server side.

output_examples.input: A platform team needs CloudBase login for users from an existing account database.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a backend ticket issuance flow, credential handling rules, and the web client handoff.

output_examples.input: An admin tool must inspect a user profile without exposing raw profile data to clients.
output_examples.output: The response recommends trusted backend lookup methods, minimal response shaping, and careful production logging.

best_practices: Use uid as the primary CloudBase user identifier in backend authorization checks.
Keep custom login credential files only on trusted servers or CloudBase functions.
Return only the user fields that clients need, and avoid full profile logging.
anti_patterns: Using this skill for frontend login UI instead of web auth guidance.
Exposing getEndUserInfo or queryUserInfo results directly to untrusted clients.
Creating custom login tickets before the external user is authenticated.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Node.js backend auth flows with the CloudBase Node SDK.

faq.question: Can it configure CloudBase login providers?
faq.answer: No. Provider setup belongs to CloudBase console or provider configuration guidance.

faq.question: Can it build a web login page?
faq.answer: No. It only covers Node-side identity, user lookup, and ticket issuance.

faq.question: Which user identifier should backend code prefer?
faq.answer: Backend code should prefer the CloudBase uid for identity and authorization decisions.

faq.question: How are custom login tickets handled?
faq.answer: Trusted Node code creates tickets after external authentication, then a client exchanges the ticket with CloudBase.

faq.question: Does it replace official SDK documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes supported patterns and expects official CloudBase docs for API details outside this scope.
